_help: §EE (5 Oct). Villages: abandoned stone-and-timber towns relit hearth by hearth. Backlog reservoir, not a build list: one archetype is built (prototype: the stream-gutter town; Villages, VillagePlan, VillageBuilder, VillageLife). Read now: prototype, plan, build, siting.weights, layout_rules (as rules VillagePlan.rules() measures), composition. The other archetypes and the specialties, lost_techniques and energy are not wired yet.

prototype._help: Design 5 Oct §EE.5: one archetype built first, the stream-gutter town (Villages, VillagePlan, VillageBuilder, VillageLife). Where it may stand: a stream (river segments stream_width_m wide and, with stream_narrower_half, no wider than the world's median river: a stream, not a great river) in stone-and-timber country (biomes, temp_c, moisture_min), on a gentle slope (grade_range over the village's ground), keep_off_m from any ruin. Each world keeps its best-scoring sites (siting.weights, at least min_score), min_spacing_m apart (scaled down on the dev stamp, never under min_spacing_floor_m), at most per_world_max. build_m / drop_m: when a village is built and freed round you.

plan._help: Design 5 Oct §EF, §EG (VillagePlan). The growth, in metres: the village's reach (radius_m), its grid (cell_m), the core square's radius and the other squares' (squares_r_m), how many squares (squares: the core counts; one is the ma void when void_kind is empty_square), lane widths (main street with its gutter, lanes, edge tracks), a house's frontage and depth, the gap between terraces in the core and at the edge, the terrace sizes allowed by ring (core_groups near the hearth, mid_groups, edge_groups: threes and fives, ones at the edge, §EG.2), meander (amplitude and wavelength of the streets' gentle bends, §EF.5), the long sightline (long_vista_m) and where a vista's focal goes (focal_angle_deg off the axis: on the thirds, §EG.2), the tower's height choices (the shortest that is seen from landmark_seen_min of the lanes: "most of the village", more than half, §EF.10).

build._help: Design 5 Oct §EE.3, §EG.3 (VillageBuilder): how a house stands on its slope (fall across its footprint: under plinth_max_m a stone plinth, under stepped_max_m stepped foundations with a dry-stone terrace below, else a timber floor on posts of their own lengths, each on a foundation stone), its walls (eave_m, focal houses taller by focal_raise_m), the dead village's overgrowth (moss, ivy over doors, roofs holed at roof_hole_share), the squares' brambles while dead (bramble_m deep, §EG.4), and the materials by rock and climate (one stone, one timber, one roof per village).

siting._doc: Feng-shui logic as a suitability score over terrain the planet already computes.

layout_rules._help: Design §EF. Applied in order after siting (§EE.3): grow the village, then compose its views (VillagePlan; each rule measured by rules(), tools/village_check.gd).

rules.do: seed at hearth/well/crossing/harbour; lay desire-line paths first; pack buildings along paths facing them, shared walls, dense core, loose edge

for each long straight sightline, ensure the far end lands on a focal point; else place one (well, lantern, feature tree, shrine, hearth house) or bend the street onto a building; distant landmarks count (borrowed scenery)
alternate narrow dark lanes with small open squares
buildings enclose courtyards and squares; no leftover open field inside the village
streets bend slightly for gradual reveals
low walls, steps, benches where light or view is good
key views get a near frame, middle subject, far backdrop
channels and streams run along streets, audible
gates, arches, paving changes between quarters
one spire, tower or great tree visible from most of the village

layout_rules.dead_village: cold hearths are placed at vista ends and in squares, so composition leads to the next fire

composition._help: Design §EG. Composition layer over §EF layout, measured by VillagePlan.rules() (tools/village_check.gd): bones, one dominant per key view (1.4 times the next), focal off-centre, no mirror (best mirror overlap under 0.4), visual-weight balance, threes and fives, one ma void, one stone/timber/roof, the dead-state refuge flip.
composition.governing: consult the genius of the place: derive everything from the site; eastern skeleton (grown, asymmetric) with western punctuation (a few axes onto landmarks)

dead_state._why: prospect without refuge reads as exposed: dread from layout (Burke's Sublime)
